narrative: Today's top tech news highlights significant advancements in AI, space exploration, and developer tools. Companies like NVIDIA and Google are pushing the boundaries of AI with new models and hardware, while SpaceX continues to secure major contracts and NASA makes strides in telescope and Mars rover missions. The developer community also sees innovation with new build systems and open-source security solutions.

highlights.title: Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm tease new N1X laptop processors
highlights.whyItMatters: This signals a major push for Arm-powered laptops with enhanced AI capabilities, potentially reshaping the PC market.

highlights.title: SpaceX awarded $6.45B in Space Force contracts ahead of IPO
highlights.whyItMatters: Securing substantial government contracts demonstrates strong financial backing and strategic importance for SpaceX's future, especially before its anticipated IPO.

highlights.title: NASA Awards Contract for Johnson Space Center Infrastructure
highlights.whyItMatters: This significant investment in infrastructure at Johnson Space Center will support future space missions and research.

highlights.title: Tiny-vLLM – high performance LLM inference engine in C++ and CUDA
highlights.whyItMatters: This open-source project offers a new solution for efficient large language model inference, beneficial for AI developers.

highlights.title: 9 demos of Gemini Omni and Gemini 3.5 in action
highlights.whyItMatters: Google showcases the advanced capabilities of its latest AI models, Gemini Omni and 3.5, indicating progress in AI development.

highlights.title: Microsoft under fire for threatening security researcher with criminal investigation
highlights.whyItMatters: This incident highlights ongoing tensions between tech giants and security researchers regarding responsible disclosure and software security.

highlights.title: Startup offers free home cleaning—if it can record it all for robot training
highlights.whyItMatters: This innovative approach to data collection for robot training raises questions about privacy and the future of service automation.

highlights.title: Cognition’s Scott Wu says AI coding agents shouldn’t replace humans
highlights.whyItMatters: A prominent figure in AI coding agents emphasizes collaboration over replacement, shaping the ongoing debate about AI's role in software development.

topics.name: AI Advancement & Integration
topics.summary: Google unveils new Gemini models and NVIDIA's CPU shows strong AI performance, while AI coding agents and robot training data collection raise questions about their societal and industry impact.

topics.name: Developer Tools & Open Source
